title: Speculative Decoding + Model Onboarding: runtime draft and rollback plan
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document captures a working design for integrating speculative decoding into the serving runtime and the associated acceptance/rollback and metrics plan for onboarding model variants. It focuses on interactions between kernel execution, the KV cache, the scheduler, and model integration lifecycle (canary -> rollout -> rollback).

Goals:
- Specify concrete semantics for speculative decoding in multi-kernel environments.
- Describe scheduling invariants so speculative batches don't violate latency SLOs for non-speculative traffic.
- Define KV cache coherence and eviction rules under speculative execution.
- Provide model acceptance criteria, telemetry, and automated rollback triggers specific to speculative changes.

High-level idea:
Speculative decoding issues a small number of ahead-of-time token continuations using a cheaper/softer model or optimized kernel path to reduce perceived latency for single-turn and streaming workloads. If the low-cost speculation matches the final generation, we serve the content immediately; otherwise we splice or replace tokens when the authoritative path completes.

Key constraints to keep in mind:
- Never expose tokens that the customer did not authorize per route-level config; speculation must be opt-in per model/route.
- Speculation must not increase P99 tail for high-priority routes above configured SLO delta.
- Cache correctness: speculative and authoritative KV cache entries must be properly versioned to avoid stale KV re-use across divergent paths.

Speculative execution modes (planned):
1) Soft-speculate (same model, cheaper kernel): run inexpensive quantized kernel to produce the next N tokens while the full-precision kernel is spinning up CPU/GPU.
2) Model-speculate (smaller model): run a distilled/smaller model to predict next tokens; later confirm with primary model.
3) Hybrid (cached prefix + soft-speculate): for requests matching cached prefixes, use KV cache + cheap kernel to extend tokens.

Runtime components touched:
- Scheduler: responsible for deciding whether to allocate a speculative task slot.
- Kernel selector: must support marking runs as speculative and exposing confidence metrics (logits gap / max-softmax / entropy).
- KV cache: must store speculative entries separately and support commit/merge/abort semantics.
- Streamer and client protocol: must support speculative token markers so downstream clients can display tentative tokens if configured.

Scheduler changes and invariants:
- Speculative work is explicitly lower priority and preemptible. Scheduler must enforce:
  - Soft cap: speculative GPU utilization <= 15% per serving-instance by default.
  - Preemption policy: if speculative work threatens SLOs for non-speculative traffic, in-progress speculative tasks should be cancelled at token-boundary (cooperative cancellation).
  - Admission control: only allow speculative runs when headroom (latency SLA margin) exists for the current traffic mix. Headroom computed from moving-window latency percentiles and configured safety margin.
- Fairness: do not allow speculative runs for premium routes unless route config enables it.

Kernel and execution semantics:
- Kernels must annotate speculative outputs with a speculation_id and a confidence vector summary (top-3 token probs, entropy).
- No in-place mutations of KV cache by speculative kernels. Speculative kernels write to a speculative-layer in-memory store keyed by (request_id, speculation_id, kv_key).
- When full model run completes, runtime compares speculative-layer entries and authoritative outputs; on match (token-level equality for the speculative window) speculative entries are committed to canonical KV cache; on mismatch the speculative-layer is discarded and authoritative entries take effect.
- To avoid double-counting usage, speculative tokens are accounted separately and can be optionally billable at a discounted speculative rate.

KV cache design for speculative flows:
- Two-layer model: committed layer (canonical) + speculative overlay(s). Overlays are ordered by speculation start time.
- Read semantics: read prefers the topmost overlay for keys that match request_id scope when reading during an in-flight speculative-confirmation round. After commit/abort, overlay entries are merged or dropped.
- Eviction: overlays have their own TTL and size cap (we cap overlay size per-request to limit memory pressure). If eviction happens before commit, speculation is treated as aborted.
- Versioning: each KV key gets a monotonic sequence id per-request; overlays include sequence ranges so merges are efficient (append-only semantics where possible).

Model onboarding, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan (speculation-aware):
- Canary policy: when onboarding a new model variant that will participate in speculation (e.g., a distilled spec model or new kernel variant), start with a 0.5% canary of traffic with speculation enabled. Two parallel flows: spec-enabled and spec-disabled to measure delta.
- Acceptance metrics (must be monitored and satisfy guardrails over 24h window unless otherwise specified):
  - Token-level divergence: fraction of speculative-token windows where authoritative tokens differ from speculative tokens (target: <= 6% for model-speculate; <= 1% for soft-speculate).
  - Commit rate: percentage of speculative windows that are committed vs aborted (target: >= 90% for soft-speculate; >= 70% for model-speculate).
  - Quality delta: A/B evals on downstream quality signals (e.g., Rouge/BLEU/LLM-specific evals on prompt sets). No statistically significant drop vs baseline (alpha=0.01).
  - Latency improvements: median client-perceived time-to-first-meaningful-token (TTFMT) should improve by >= 8% for spec-enabled traffic.
  - Resource overhead: additional GPU/VRAM utilization attributable to speculation <= 10% of baseline capacity at canary scale.
  - Error surface: speculative-specific errors (overlay evictions, preempted specs) must be < 0.1% of requests.
- Safety gates (automatic):
  - If token-level divergence > 10% over 1h, immediate rollback of speculation path for that model.
  - If commit rate < configured minimum for 30m (rolling), disable speculation for the model variant.
  - If P99 latency for non-spec traffic increases by > 5% absolute, preempt all speculation in impacted region/instance.

Rollback and canary isolation details:
- Rollback granularity: model_variant, region, pool, route. Can roll back speculation codepath for a model without removing the model entirely (configurable).
- Automated rollback flow:
  1) Detection triggers via metrics alerting rules.
  2) Orchestration layer marks the model variant/speculation flag as disabled and pushes policy to router/scheduler.
  3) Instances gracefully cancel speculative in-flight tasks (finish current token then abort speculative continuation) and invalidate overlays.
  4) Telemetry events emitted: speculation.rollback.triggered, speculation.rollback.completed, speculation.rollback.reason.
- Human-in-the-loop: we add a manual-confirm rollback for anything that affects >5% of traffic; automatic rollback for small canaries is allowed.

Observability and telemetry (instrumentation plan):
- Core events (per-request dimensioned):
  - speculation.request.start {speculation_id, model_variant, mode, route, route_tier}
  - speculation.run.complete {speculation_id, outcome: committed|aborted|preempted|evicted, commit_latency_ms}
  - speculation.confidence.summary {entropy, max_logit_margin}
  - kv.overlay.merge {speculation_id, keys_merged}
  - speculation.rollback.{triggered|completed}
- Metrics to be derived:
  - speculation.commit_rate (per-model, per-route)
  - speculation.divergence_rate (per-model)
  - speculation.latency_benefit.p50/p95/p99 (client perceived)
  - speculation.cpu_gpu_overhead_pct (per-node)
- Dashboards and alerts:
  - Canary dashboard showing divergence vs quality evals, commit rate, and resource overhead.
  - SLO alerts: speculative_preemption_rate > threshold, divergence spikes, commit_rate drop.

Example request flow (simplified):
1) Request arrives, route config indicates speculation allowed and selects mode=soft-speculate.
2) Scheduler checks headroom, admits speculative job into low-prio queue and allocates a quantized kernel slot.
3) Spec kernel runs and writes overlay entries for KV keys and emits speculation.request.start. Client receives tentative tokens with speculation markers.
4) Primary model kernel begins; reads committed cache + overlays. It produces authoritative tokens.
5) Primary kernel compares the token window with speculative output; if identical: overlay is committed; telemetry emits speculation.run.complete outcome=committed and overlay merge. If not identical: outcome=aborted and speculative tokens are replaced client-side where protocol allows, or authoritative tokens are appended with correction metadata.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for overlay merge/abort semantics and eviction behavior.
- Integration tests simulating concurrent spec and authoritative runs with simulated preemption and cache eviction.
- Load tests at 0.5%, 5%, and 20% speculation intensity measuring latency tail and memory pressure.
- Golden prompt set: curated set of production prompts for automated divergence and quality checks.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- UI behavior: what is the default client experience when speculative tokens are later aborted? (options: visual rollback, replace text, show correction markers).
- Billing model: do we bill speculative tokens? If yes, at what discount? Need product/finance input.
- How to define per-route headroom safely for mixed-traffic environments? Propose starting conservative and exposing a route knob to opt into higher speculation caps.
- Kernel contract: how detailed should the confidence summary be for effective commit heuristics? (more telemetry increases overhead).

Appendix: proposed rollout timeline (high level)
- Week 0-2: implement kernel and KV overlay primitives + unit tests.
- Week 3-4: local integration, overlay merging, and synthetic load tests.
- Week 5: internal dogfood on dev cluster with opt-in routes.
- Week 6-8: 0.5% canary for model variants + dashboards and alerts.
- Week 9-12: expand canary to 5% and run extended quality evals; iterate on acceptance thresholds.

Action items:
- Product: confirm billing stance for speculative tokens (assigned: Mariana).
- Platform/SRE: define safe default headroom calculation and add scheduler admission control hooks (assigned: Evan).
- Serving runtime: prototype overlay KV API and speculative annotations in kernel interface (assigned: Daniel).

If we want, I can break this into a narrower PRD focusing only on KV overlay APIs or only on the scheduler admission control. For now this is intended as a cross-team working draft to iterate against concrete impl PRs.

End of document.
